operator_request: Investigate hierarchical layouts, hypergraphs and TurboQuant using deep research, the web and arXiv
fallback_reason: Fable and Opus OAuth sessions expired; the same consultation continued through its configured fallback
questions: Can a small resident hierarchy select physically contiguous cells with enough boundary coverage and bounded S3 fetch waves?
Does overlapping cell membership improve coverage enough to justify duplication and mutation cost?
Does TurboQuant or RaBitQ improve compressed scoring at the same candidate coverage and byte budget?
What are the full RAM, scratch, generation pinning, maintenance, concurrency and lifecycle cost formulas at 1M, 10M and 100M?
What is the cheapest decisive no-cloud falsifier before changing the format?
initial_source_limitations: Quantizer distortion guarantees do not establish routing coverage or end-to-end ANN recall

The hypergraph paper's complementary candidate-generation mechanism is a useful hypothesis for D768, D1000 and other dimensions. Its D384 relevant-pair Hit@10 numbers require a transfer test before being reported as our exact-neighbor recall@100 or S3 cold tails; differing dimensions are not a rejection criterion
Hypergraph candidate generation depends on embedding-coordinate activation distributions; combining it with a random rotation requires a separate selectivity and coverage test
Turbopuffer's published 100B architecture discussion includes SSD-resident deployments; it does not establish a matched fully cold S3 result
The current whole-directory resident prototype has no measured 100M admission or serving result
required_output: Primary-source evidence table, competing layouts and query DAGs, explicit scale and maintenance formulas, counterexamples, recommended decision and one cheap falsifier
